passage:
Class teacher's note.

Two teachers and several students mentioned to me this week that Afreen has been saying Zubin's science project was bought online and that he only took the class monitor role by flattering me. Zubin came to see me on Thursday. He was upset but calm. He brought his dated drafts, his handwritten notes and photos of the model at each stage, and asked me to look at them. He did not name anyone or say anything unkind about Afreen. I told him I believed the evidence and would clarify facts with the teachers concerned. I have also spoken to Afreen separately about the effect of rumours, without accusing her of anything I cannot prove. Zubin has asked that no one retaliate.

qa.q: What did Zubin bring to his meeting with the class teacher?
qa.a: His dated drafts, his handwritten notes and photos of the model at each stage.

qa.q: How was Zubin feeling when he came to the teacher, and what shows his approach?
qa.a: Upset but calm. He did not name anyone or say anything unkind about Afreen and stuck to the evidence, with no plan for retaliation.

qa.q: Why does the teacher's approach of speaking to Afreen separately help?
qa.a: It addresses the rumours without accusing her of anything unprovable, and it keeps the matter fair. The teacher can clear up facts with the other teachers at the same time.

qa.q: How might Afreen see being spoken to by the teacher?
qa.a: Possibly with defensiveness or unease. The teacher didn't accuse her of anything unprovable, so she might also feel she has a chance to stop.

grounding: A rival spreads doubts; the protagonist calmly brings his record to adults and avoids retaliation.

passage:
In Bhadrachalam's only English-medium school, everyone knew Francis and Nandini would fight for the science exhibition slot at district level. When Francis's rain-gauge model was picked, the whispers began within a week.

"Sir, his model is the same as one on a video site," Nandini told the physics teacher in the corridor, loudly enough for the Class 9 line to hear. By Friday two of Francis's friends were asking if it was true.

Francis's first thought was to tell everyone about the time Nandini's project leaned on her brother's help. He sat on the temple steps near his house that evening and let the idea go.

On Monday he carried his rough notebook to the staffroom: three weeks of sketches, the failed funnel design, the bill for the plastic tubing from Raju's hardware shop. "Sir, I heard there's doubt about my model. These are my drafts." The teacher turned the pages slowly and nodded.

Francis didn't say one word about Nandini.

qa.q: What did Francis carry to the staffroom on Monday?
qa.a: Francis carried his rough notebook to the staffroom.

qa.q: What was Francis feeling on the temple steps that evening?
qa.a: Francis felt angry and tempted to hit back by telling everyone about Nandini's project, but calmed enough to let that idea go.
Showing the teacher his drafts worked, because it corrected the facts calmly with proof and kept Francis's own record clean.

qa.q: How might the physics teacher see Francis after looking at the notebook?
qa.a: The teacher likely trusts Francis more, seeing weeks of honest effort, and may start to question the story Nandini spread.

grounding: It shows a teen whose rival spreads doubts about him to a teacher and friends, and who calmly corrects the facts with an adult while avoiding retaliation.

passage:
At the swim club in Busan, Layla noticed the change before anyone said anything. Coach Park stopped giving her the fast lane. Two girls from the relay team went quiet when she walked into the changing room.

It was Jin. Layla found out from a younger swimmer: Jin had been telling people that Layla skipped the dawn sessions and only turned up for time trials. It wasn't true. Layla had missed one Tuesday, for a dentist visit, and had told the front desk.

That night she wanted to message the whole team about Jin's own late arrivals. She typed it out. Then she deleted it.

The next morning, before warm-up, she asked Coach Park for two minutes. "I heard there's a worry that I miss dawn sessions. I've only missed one this term. The front desk has the sign-in sheet." The coach checked it that afternoon.

Layla kept arriving at five-forty, every day, and kept swimming. The lane came back the following week.

qa.q: What time did Layla keep arriving at the pool?
qa.a: Layla kept arriving at five-forty, every day.

qa.q: Why did Layla type a message about Jin and then delete it?
qa.a: Layla felt hurt and angry enough to want revenge, but on reflection didn't want to become the person spreading stories.

qa.q: What could Layla do if Jin keeps spreading rumours?
qa.a: Layla could keep a clean attendance record and calmly go back to Coach Park with facts, rather than confronting Jin in front of the team.

qa.q: What would change if Layla had sent the message to the whole team?
qa.a: The team might have seen two swimmers trading accusations, which could have made Coach Park doubt both of them and hidden the fact that Layla was telling the truth.

grounding: It shows a teen whose rival spreads doubts about her to a coach and teammates, and who keeps her record clean, calmly corrects the facts and avoids retaliation.
